title: Cloudflare agents reliability benchmark — Agents SDK vs DOs vs Workflows vs Queues vs Sandbox
description: Evidence-backed comparison of Cloudflare Agents SDK, Durable Objects, Workflows, Queues (product), and Sandbox SDK across reliability dimensions: persistence, checkpoints, retries, DLQ, idempotency, outbox, websockets, and incident coverage.

agents_comparison.durable_objects: Primitive backing storage; single-threaded per ID
agents_comparison.workflows: Not session-first; step state persisted per workflow
agents_comparison.sandbox: Workspace FS depends on workspace type (Local persistent, Docker ephemeral)

agents_comparison.agents_sdk: runFiber/startFiber with stash() and onFiberRecovered hooks; app resumes from snapshots
agents_comparison.durable_objects: Can store snapshots per object for resume
agents_comparison.queues: No checkpointing primitives; messages are units of work

agents_comparison.agents_sdk: retry helpers but no built-in DLQ for internal queue; app must persist failed items
agents_comparison.durable_objects: coordinator for dedupe; no DLQ by itself
agents_comparison.workflows: per-step retries configurable; errored workflow shown in UI
agents_comparison.sandbox: No delivery DLQ; retries must be orchestrated

agents_comparison.agents_sdk: idempotencyKey on startFiber; ledger patterns for tool runs but app must implement handlers
agents_comparison.durable_objects: single-threaded DO is ideal for idempotency keys
agents_comparison.queues: use DO/KV for idempotency with queue messages
agents_comparison.sandbox: tool outputs must be written to durable store by integrator

agents_comparison.agents_sdk: Connection state persisted; session history durable; per-client ACKs left to app
agent-tool ledger + detached runs but handlers must be idempotent
agents_comparison.workflows: can call external tool endpoints as steps
agents_comparison.sandbox: Designed for isolated exec (STI) but orchestration external

incident_matrix.notes: Agents SDK provides session tables and compaction; DO SQLite default persists session state.
Agents provide runs/fibers and agent-tool ledger; resume/compensate policy is app-defined.
Retry primitives exist but DLQ/dedupe remain app concerns; prefer Queues for high throughput.
DO alarms + runFiber recovery and SDK defensive measures present.
SDK persists outputs but per-client ACK and final-channel delivery semantics must be implemented by app.

recommendations_timeline.action: Use Agents SDK for session-backed chat and light background work; avoid head-of-line tasks and test _flushQueue behavior.
For long-running multi-step orchestration migrate core pipelines to Workflows and use Agents for UI/state; or use Queues + DO for high-throughput ingestion.
Implement DLQ persistence for failed agent-queue items and an outbox DO pattern for delivery ack.

evidence_table.note: Core repo: sessions, fibers, queues, agent-tool ledger
